drhp.business: Camex Limited is engaged in a multi-segment business comprising Dyes and Chemicals, Metals, Fiber Glass and Others. Its established line is dyes and chemicals sold largely into textile and allied colorant end-uses, an industry the company describes as concentrated in Gujarat and dependent on imported intermediates. During the year under review the company commenced a Fiber Glass business, having purchased industrial land at Changodar (Taluka Sanand, District Ahmedabad) on 16th April 2024 to carry on manufacturing of Fiberglass CSM products and equivalent products.

risks.note: MD&A Risks and Areas of Concern states dyes and pigments are prepared from chemicals primarily derived from basic petrochemicals (benzene, toluene, xylene and naphthalene), so 'input costs are volatile given that they are crude oil derivatives'. The MD&A separately flags that volatile raw material prices in the fiberglass business reduce profit margins and create unstable pricing for customers, and that a spike in raw material prices is threatening the Gujarat dyes industry. With operating margin in low single digits, input-cost swings pass straight through to profitability.

The MD&A outlook notes delayed shipments from China threaten the dyes and dyestuff industry in Gujarat, that local dyestuff units are heavily dependent on imports of several raw materials including chemicals and intermediates from China, and that industry players fear disruption could lead to 25% of dyestuff making units in the state closing. Camex is a Gujarat-based dyes and chemicals manufacturer exposed to the same sourcing base.
risks.risk: Dependence on imported Chinese intermediates and supply-chain disruption

risks.note: Stated twice - in the MD&A Risks and Areas of Concern section and again in the discussion on financial performance: 'depreciation in the rupee as compared to US$ may have some effect on the Company's business'. It is the only currency risk management explicitly names, and it sits alongside directors' hope of better results in the current financial year.
risks.risk: Rupee depreciation against the US dollar

risks.note: The MD&A notes domestic environmental issues and regulations would restrict supply growth from SMEs, and that demand would increasingly be met by large players because they can install the effluent systems required to comply with regulations - a structural disadvantage for a smaller manufacturer. For fiberglass the report states manufacturing involves chemicals and emissions that may face stricter environmental controls, naming waste disposal, VOC emissions and compliance costs as challenges the company might face.
risks.risk: Environmental regulation and compliance cost across both segments

risks.note: MD&A Opportunities and Threats states that competition from China in the export market would impact the smaller players, and that the major dye and dye intermediates importing countries - Turkey, Indonesia, Bangladesh and Italy - had seen lockdowns and restrictions that pulled exports down. India and Indonesia are also described as taking the lead in dye manufacturing, adding to competitive pressure.
risks.risk: Export-market competition from China affecting smaller players

risks.note: The MD&A states competition from alternative materials may affect the revenue of fiberglass, specifically naming carbon fiber, aluminium composites, PVC and advanced plastics. This risk attaches to the segment the Company has just entered and into which it has committed industrial land at Changodar, so it bears on the payback of the diversification itself.
risks.risk: Substitution risk in the new fiberglass segment

risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter (Note 35) records that a fire occurred at the Company's wax plant at Ankleshwar in July 2024, damaging property, plant and equipment and causing consequential losses. The claim was settled in the current financial year with a surplus over the earlier estimate recognised as an Exceptional Item, but the event demonstrates single-site physical risk at a chemical manufacturing operation; the Directors' Report notes buildings, plant and machinery and stocks are adequately insured.
risks.risk: Plant fire / physical asset loss at manufacturing sites

risks.note: The MD&A ties dye demand to textiles (the major application for dyes) and to paints, coatings and construction expenditure, and ties the fiberglass outlook to construction, infrastructure, renewable energy, automotive and industrial sectors. It also notes printing-ink demand is being restrained as information publication moves to electronic form. Both segments therefore depend on the same discretionary construction and consumption cycle.
risks.risk: End-market cyclicality concentrated in textiles and construction
